A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safe-FedLLM work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-training experiments on Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B, including safety, utility, detection, efficiency and malicious-client-ratio results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports results for three comparison methods in Table 2.

M1.justification: The probe, three defense mechanisms, early freezing, round skipping and weighted aggregation remain unchanged. Explicit normalized-feature notation in v2 reflects L2 normalization already documented in v1 Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use LMSYS-Chat and WildChat with BeaverTails and MaliciousGen, evaluate safety on AdvBench and utility using MT-1, and retain the same malicious-client-ratio scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds DnC, FLAME and LASA across all four Llama3.1-8B dataset combinations, substantially broadening the evaluated defenses. Matching Krum rows are relabeled Multi-Krum with unchanged scores. The Qwen2.5-7B comparison in Table 9 gains no additional comparator.

E3.justification: The stated splits, metrics, 500 samples per client, 100 rounds, three sampled clients per round, ten local steps and defense hyperparameters are retained. Newly specified optimizer, learning rate and quantization details do not establish changes to the existing experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The LoRA separability visualization, precision-over-rounds analysis, attack-intensity experiments and appendix detection results are retained. No new ablation, robustness test or supplementary analytical question is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the shared-initialization requirement and fixed initial LoRA parameters. Neither adds repeated-run counts, numerical seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds results for DnC, FLAME and LASA; all matched pre-existing table values remain unchanged. On BeaverTails & LMSYS-Chat, LASA's Rule score of 61.73 exceeds Krum/Multi-Krum's 60.19, changing the strongest baseline there, while Shadow-Level remains at 91.92. Other retained findings are stable.

T1.justification: The mathematical procedures and assumptions are retained. Normalized-feature notation in Equations 3–4, the client subscript in Equation 8 and replacement of repeated formulas by cross-references in Appendix C clarify existing mathematics without adding or revising theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract softens the benign-performance claim from 'without compromising performance' to maintaining competitive performance. The introduction changes the claimed detection target from malicious samples to malicious updates. The main vulnerability, separability and defense contributions remain.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 scopes the retained 52.7% improvement to the Rule comparison against Multi-Krum on BeaverTails & LMSYS-Chat and drops the 'second-best' description, appropriately accommodating LASA's added result. Appendix B also qualifies constant-rate stabilization as reducing rather than preventing drift. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies ten total clients, random client sampling, AdamW_bnb_8bit, a learning rate of 5×10^-5 and 8-bit base-model quantization. These improve implementation disclosure without demonstrating changed settings. The code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 replaces FD-LoRA/FedLoRA citations with broader federated graph-learning, clustering and knowledge-alignment references. New FLAME, LASA and optimizer references support the expanded material. The central positioning of Safe-FedLLM remains unchanged; numerous publication-metadata updates concern retained works.

P1.justification: Extensive prose editing spans the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, results discussion and appendices. Terminology is systematically revised from LoRA weights to updates, sentences and cross-references are clarified, author information is expanded and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains comparator rows; Figures 1 and 3 receive labeling and presentation revisions. Figure 4 is redrawn with different typography and axis styling and relocated, while retaining its plotted findings. Other tables undergo limited spacing, formatting and placement changes.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the main comparison through three additional defenses, discloses useful reproduction settings and makes the performance and detection claims more precise. These changes improve assessability and clarity. The gains are bounded: the added comparisons cover only Llama3.1-8B, while the underlying method, task coverage and robustness evidence remain unchanged.
